one_line: Heir of Venad and future founder of Travancore, navigating a deadly succession crisis in early 18th‑century Kerala.

appearance.age_look: Looks about 20–22, lean but wiry, with the light athletic build of a young swordsman used to constant movement and narrow escapes.
appearance.face: Oval face with warm medium-brown Kerala complexion, sharp straight nose, defined jaw, slightly arched brows and large focused anime-style eyes; a thin tilak of sandal paste on the forehead; default expression calm but alert, with a hint of wary determination as if always scanning for danger.
appearance.hair: Thick black hair oiled and neatly combed back into a low knot at the back of the head (traditional chignon) wrapped in a narrow white cloth band, with a few controlled strands framing the temples; no crown, only a simple gold forehead chain resting just above the tilak.
appearance.costume: He wears an early 18th‑century Venad royal outfit: a knee-length off‑white mundu (wrapped lower garment) with a narrow maroon and gold kasavu border, wrapped securely and pleated in front; over his torso a fitted long-sleeved cotton angarakha-style upper garment in deep teal, crossing left over right and tied with concealed strings, its edges piped in muted gold; a lightweight cream-colored kasavu shawl with thin gold borders draped from the left shoulder across the chest and tucked at the waist, ready to be rewrapped for disguise; on his feet simple dark-brown leather sandals; jewellery is modest—small round gold ear studs, a single thin gold chain with a tiny Vishnu pendant, and a simple gold bangle on the right wrist—signaling royalty but not ostentatious display during a crisis.
appearance.signature: A slim, slightly curved steel sword of the type used in 18th‑century Kerala, with a plain iron hilt wrapped in dark-brown leather and a small knuckle-guard, sheathed in a dark teakwood scabbard with subtle brass fittings, worn at his left hip by a plain brown leather belt.

ref_desc: Young Marthanda Varma has a medium-brown oval face with a sandal tilak, black hair in a low knot with a white band and gold forehead chain, wearing a deep-teal angarakha, off‑white kasavu mundu with maroon-gold border, cream shawl, simple gold jewellery and sandals, carrying a slim curved steel sword in a dark wooden scabbard at his left hip.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of young Marthanda Varma from early 18th‑century Kerala: a lean 20‑something prince with an oval medium-brown face, large serious eyes, straight nose, defined jaw and a thin sandalwood tilak on his forehead, his thick black hair oiled back into a low knot wrapped with a narrow white cloth band and a simple gold forehead chain resting above the tilak. Show him in a historically accurate Venad royal outfit: a knee-length off‑white mundu with a narrow maroon and muted-gold kasavu border, neatly pleated in front; a fitted long-sleeved deep‑teal cotton angarakha-style upper garment crossing left over right with subtle muted-gold piping; and a light cream kasavu shawl with thin gold borders draped from his left shoulder across his chest and tucked at the waist, suggesting it could be rearranged as a disguise cloak. Put simple dark-brown leather sandals on his feet and give him modest jewellery only—small round gold ear studs, a thin gold chain with a tiny Vishnu pendant, and a single gold bangle on his right wrist—to convey understated royal status during a dangerous succession crisis. At his left hip, attached by a plain brown leather belt, show his signature weapon: a slim, slightly curved steel sword appropriate to 18th‑century Kerala, with a plain iron hilt wrapped in dark-brown leather and a small knuckle-guard, housed in a dark teakwood scabbard with subtle brass fittings. Use a palette dominated by off‑white, deep teal, maroon, muted gold and dark brown, and present him from multiple angles with consistent face, hair, costume details and sword design, his default expression calm but wary as if ready to react to an ambush.
